newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DITKA OFFICIALLY NAMED HEAD COACH OF SAINTS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DITKA OFFICIALLY NAMED HEAD COACH OF SAINTS.

text.p: The New Orleans Saints made it official on Tuesday, hiring Mike Ditka as head coach.
Ditka, who coached the Chicago Bears to a Super Bowl victory in New Orleans following the 1985 season and left the sidelines in 1992, will be tackling a difficult assignment.
The Saints have failed to win a single playoff game since joining the NFL in 1967.
"I want to create a greater sense of pride in this organisation," Ditka said at a news conference Tuesday. "It won't come easy. Nothing good in this life ever does."
Ditka will be facing a daunting task in trying to turn around the Saints, who did not have a winning season until 1987.
Excluding the Baltimore Ravens, whose previous records in Cleveland are not counted among NFL statistics, the Saints are the only franchise without a playoff victory, going 0-4.

Former coach Jim Mora, the only coach with a winning record with the Saints (93-78 in 10-plus years), resigned after a 2-6 start this season. Rick Venturi took over for Mora and went 1-7 as interim coach.

New Orleans drew just 301,998 fans this past season, an average of 37,750 per game. That figure was off 25 percent from last season as the Saints posted their fourth consecutive non-winning campaign and their worst since going 1-15 in 1980.
"If you live in the past, you die in the past," Ditka said of the Saints' history. "We can't erase the past, we just have to prepare for what we can do in the future."

Ditka said he already has begun to assemble a staff of assistants, but refused to make any of the appointments public. The Chicago Sun-Times reported Monday that former Bears assistants Danny Abramowicz and Zaven Yaralian are among those hired.
Ditka, who was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1988, most recently served as an NFL broadcaster for NBC Sports.

Ditka coached the Bears from 1982-92, compiling a 112-68 record, including a 6-6 playoff mark. Aside from the strike-shortened 1982 season, he had only two losing seasons (1989, 1992) and recorded seven seasons of at least 10 wins. The gruff Ditka won six NFC Central titles and advanced to three NFC Championship games.

In 1985, Chicago ripped apart the league with a 15-1 record, losing only to Miami after a 12-0 start. The Bears won both their NFC playoff games by shutout and advanced to Super Bowl XXI in New Orleans, where they pummeled the New England Patriots 46-10.
Ditka was named Coach of the Year in 1988, posting a 12-4 record despite a mid-season heart attack. He holds the NFL mark for most wins in a four-year span with 52, done from 1985-88.

As a player, he was named NFL Rookie of the Year in 1961, following a season in which he caught 56 passes as a tight end. He appeared in the Pro Bowl in all six seasons he was with the Bears (1961-1966). He played two years with the Eagles and four with Cowboys, earning a Super Bowl ring after the 1971 campaign, before retiring following the 1972 season.
